newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia corn importers brace for heavy losses.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia corn importers brace for heavy losses.

text.p: Malaysian corn importers were bracing for heavy losses on Tuesday as prices continued to fall in a market overloaded with maize, trade sources said.
A new arrival of 50,000 tonnes of corn in the last week added to a stockpile of around 100,000 tonnes to squeeze importers' margins further.
Losses would heighten by end of June with the expected arrival of another 200,000 tonnes, trade sources said.
They said compared to last's week price of 385-390 ringgit, bulk corn, ex-factories/godowns in Malaysia's central region, was trading at 380-385 ringgit a tonne C&F this week.
"I think importers will be looking at further losses of 20 to 30 ringgit per tonne by the end of June," said the trading manager of a flour mill in Kuala Lumpur.
The glut is the result of huge positions taken in the last three months by importers excited with the entry of Chinese corn into the market, grain dealers said.
They said warehouses were already facing a critical shortage of space.
"Importers are scrambling for every little inch of storage space they can find," said a dealer. "Some are looking for offshore storage facilities, others are trying to delay the arrivals.
"The results will be extra cost," added the dealer.
Traders said the glut could last until the end of July or early August and no fresh corn orders were expected until then.
"An equilibrium will have to be struck here," said one source.
"A" grade wheat in bags was unchanged at 730 ringgit. "B" grade wheat was steady at 430 ringgit.
Soymeal was maintained at 880 ringgit for the local material and 870 for the imported stuff.
